    South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
    (SAARC)

           What:

            SAARC was formed in 1985 in Dhaka Conference as a regional intergovernmental
                 organization for South Asian cooperation. Bangladesh President Ziaur Rahman proposed
                 the idea.

               Tell me more:




Regional Organisation                                                                                                               8

SAFTA

                 The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) was launched in 2006 under SAARC to
                     abolish trade and tariff restrictions in the region and eventually create a common market
                    with a common currency.

            SAARC SUMMITS

               SAARC summits are generally held every two years and hosted by member states in
                     alphabetical order, with the host country assuming the Chair of the Association.

                 The 1st SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh in 1985.

     Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)

           What:

            ASEAN was established as a regional intergovernmental organization on 8 August 1967 in
               Bangkok, Thailand, through the signing of the ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration).

               Tell me more:

              The Foreign Ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand
                signed the ASEAN Declaration at the Department of Foreign Affairs building in Bangkok,
                 Thailand.

              The First ASEAN Summit was held in Bali, Indonesia on 23-24 February 1976.

    Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)

           What:

              The Shanghai Five mechanism was formed as a confidence-building forum to demilitarize
                borders among China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan.

                   In 2001, Uzbekistan joined the group, and on 15 June 2001, the organization was renamed
               as the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

               Tell me more:

                    Official working languages of SCO are Chinese (Mandarin) and Russian.

                   In 2017, India and Pakistan were admitted as full members.

     Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)

           What:

              The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) was established on 7 March 1997 as an inter-
               governmental organisation to strengthen regional cooperation and sustainable development
                    in the Indian Ocean region.

               Tell me more:

              The vision for IORA originated during a visit by late President Nelson Mandela of South
                  Africa to India in 1995.

                       Initially, it was known as the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Co-operation.





Regional Organisation                                                                                                               9

The Council of (Foreign) Ministers is the highest decision-making body of IORA and usually
                holds annual meetings. It elects the Chair and Vice Chair of the Association for a two-year
               term

     Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)

           What:

                 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) is a forum of Pacific Rim economies that
               promotes free trade in the Asia-Pacific region.

               Tell me more:

                  Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke proposed the idea of APEC, which led to the first
            APEC meeting in Canberra, Australia, in November 1989, chaired by Australian Foreign
                   Affairs Minister Gareth Evans.

                  India is not a part of the APEC because it does not border the Pacific Ocean. However, India
             was invited to be an observer for the first time in November 2011.

    Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC)

             FIPIC is a multinational grouping developed in 2014 for cooperation between India and 14
              Pacific Island Nations. All heads of government of member countries met in FIJI in 2014 where
                  first annual summit was conceptualized.

           Under India’s Act East Policy, India is strengthening relations with Pacific island nations through
             cooperation in blue economy, energy, mining, IT, healthcare, fishing, and marine research.
           These countries also support ISRO by helping monitor Indian rocket launches.

            14 Pacific Island Nations - Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue,
           Samoa, Solomon Islands, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu.

    BRICS

           What:

              The term “BRIC” was coined in 2001 by economist Jim O’Neill of Goldman Sachs for Brazil,
                 Russia, India, and China; these countries began regular informal diplomatic coordination in
               2006, held their first BRIC Summit in 2009, and were joined by South Africa in 2010.

          Why:

              BRICS countries account for 42% of the world’s population and around 20% of global GDP,
              making it an influential group of major developing economies.

               Tell me more:

                During the 6th BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014, BRICS established two
                 financing facilities - New Development Bank with an initial capital of US$50 billion and
               Contingency Reserve Arrangement (CRA) with US$100 billion fund. Both function
                 independently.

    New Development Bank





Regional Organisation                                                                                                              10

What:

              The New Development Bank (NDB), formerly called the BRICS Development Bank, is a
                   multilateral development bank, established to finance infrastructure and sustainable
               development projects in BRICS and other developing economies.

               Tell me more:

                           It started with a capital of US$50 billion, with Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa
                 contributing US$10 billion each. The bank’s capital is planned to increase to US$100 billion.

      Contingent Reserve Arrangement

           What:

              The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) is a US $100 billion financial support
              mechanism created to help BRICS countries during global financial or currency crises.

               Tell me more:

                           It provides emergency liquidity support when member countries face pressure on their
                 currencies due to global economic instability. The CRA is considered an alternative to IMF
                support and reflects growing cooperation among developing countries.

                           It is a financial arrangement jointly managed by the BRICS member countries through their
                  central banks and finance ministries.

     Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
    (OPEC)

           What:

              The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) was established as an
                intergovernmental organization at the Baghdad Conference in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait,
                Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela to coordinate petroleum policies and stabilize global oil
                markets.

               Tell me more:

            OPEC+ is a group formed in 2016 when OPEC joined with 10 other oil-producing countries
                  to coordinate oil production and stabilize global oil prices after falling prices caused by
                   rising U.S. shale oil production.

    European Union

           What:

              The European Union (EU) is a political and economic union of 27 countries that allows free
             movement of people, goods, services, and capital among member states. The UK has
               withdrawn from the EU.

          Why:

              The European Union originated from efforts to prevent wars in Europe after World War II.
                Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands founded the European





Regional Organisation                                                                                                              11

Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) in 1952 to promote economic integration.

              The Maastricht Treaty established the European Union in 1993.

               Tell me more:

              The Euro was introduced in 1999 and fully implemented in 2002.

              The European Central Bank (ECB) manages the Euro and implements the EU’s economic
              and monetary policies. The EU is also the world’s largest trading bloc and largest exporter
                 of manufactured goods and services.

           European Union Bodies

               There are 15 bodies under the aegis of the European Union.

            Some important organizations under EU: -

                  Law-making: There are 3 main institutions involved in EU legislation:

                        the European Parliament, which represents the EU’s citizens and is directly elected
                     by them.

                        the European Council, which represents the governments of the individual member
                         countries. The Presidency of the Council is shared by the member states on a
                          rotating basis.

                        the European Commission, which represents the interests of the Union as a whole.

                      Financial institutions:

                        the European Central Bank is responsible for European monetary policy.

                        the European Investment Bank finances EU investment projects and helps small
                      businesses through the European Investment Fund.

     Organization for Economic Cooperation and
    Development (OECD)

           What:

              The OECD is an intergovernmental economic organization of 38 developed countries,
               founded in 1961 to promote economic progress and world trade.

               Tell me more:

                           It evolved from the Organisation for European Economic Cooperation (OEEC), which was
                 established in 1948 to implement the Marshall Plan for Europe’s reconstruction after World
             War II.

              Most OECD member countries are high income economies with a very high Human
               Development Index (HDI).

     Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)

           What:

                 Established in 1961, the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is a group of countries not formally
                 aligned with major power blocs such as the USA or former Soviet Union, and its




Regional Organisation                                                                                                              12

Coordinating Bureau is based at the United Nations headquarters in New York.

          Why:

           NAM was formed to keep developing countries independent from both Western and
                Eastern power blocs during the Cold War period.

               Tell me more:

              The term “Non-Aligned” was first used by Indian diplomat V. K. Krishna Menon at the United
                Nations in 1953.

               Founding Members -

                    Jawaharlal Nehru — India’s first Prime Minister

                  Sukarno — Indonesia’s first President

                 Gamal Abdel Nasser — Egypt’s second President

               Kwame Nkrumah — Ghana’s first President

                    Josip Broz Tito — President of Yugoslavia

              5 principles of NAM (Panchsheel):

                   Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty.

                   Mutual non-aggression.

                   Mutual non-interference in domestic affairs.

                     Equality and mutual benefit.

                   Peaceful co-existence.

              The first Conference of Non-Aligned Countries was held in Belgrade, Serbia, in 1961, and in
               October 2021, Belgrade hosted the High-Level Commemorative Meeting marking its 60th
                 anniversary.

    G-7

         G 7 is an international informal finance group consisting 7 industrialized nations Canada,
            France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

         G 7 was established in 1975 to facilitate economic cooperation among the world’s largest
               industrial nations.

           The G8 was reformatted as G7 from 2014 due to the suspension of Russia's participation

         G8 was an inter-governmental political forum from 1997 until 2014.

           The European Union (EU) is a ‘non-enumerated member’ of the G7, meaning it is a full member
                in practice but is not counted in the official name or the group’s leadership rotation.

    G-20

         G20 is an international forum for governments and central bank governors from 20 major
            economies.





Regional Organisation                                                                                                              13

It was founded in 1999 with the aim of studying, reviewing, and promoting high-level
             discussion of policy issues pertaining to the promotion of international financial stability.

         Note: G-20 and G-7 do not have permanent secretariate. Without a permanent secretariat, the
       G20 and G7 function via annual rotating presidencies, where the host nation finances and
       manages all logistics, agenda-setting, and administrative tasks for that year.

    G-77 (Group of 77)

           What:

              The Group of 77 (G77) is the largest intergovernmental organization of developing countries
                    in the United Nations, formed to promote the collective economic interests of developing
                  nations, strengthen their negotiating capacity on international economic issues, and
              enhance South-South cooperation for development.

               Tell me more:

              G-77 was established on 15 June 1964 at the end of the first session of the United Nations
               Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) in Geneva.

              The first meeting of the G77 was held in Algiers (Algeria) in October 1967 where “Charter of
                  Algiers” was adopted.

                 “Charter of Algiers” describes the institutional structure of the G-77.

              The charter facilitated the creation of Chapters of the G77 in difference countries with
                 Liaison offices in Geneva (UNCTAD), Nairobi (UNEP), Paris (UNESCO), Rome (FAO/IFAD),
               Vienna (UNIDO), and the Group of 24 (G-24) in Washington, D.C. (IMF and World Bank).

                Although the members of the G-77 have increased to 134 countries, the original name was
                 retained due to its historic significance.

           Knowledge Nuggets:

               South-South cooperation is a framework under which two more developing countries,
                 located in the Global South (or Southern Hemisphere of the Globe), cooperate for mutual
                growth. The South-South cooperation facilitates knowledge sharing, technology transfers,
              and collaboration for development and resolving common issues for mutual benefit.

              The Buenos Aires Plan of Action for Promoting and Implementing Technical Cooperation
            among Developing Countries (BAPA) conceptualized and formalized the South-South
                Cooperation on September 18, 1978 in Buenos Aires, Argentine. BAPA was adopted by 138
           UN Member States.

             BAPA facilitates the technical cooperation among the developing countries in the Global
                South.

              The division of “North” and “South” is used to refer to the social, economic and political
                 differences that exist between developed countries (North) and developing countries
                  (South). Under North-South Cooperation, a developed country partners with a developing
                 country. In contrast to this, in the Triangular Cooperation, two countries from the South and
              one from the North (which can also be country or an international organization) partner for
               development.





Regional Organisation                                                                                                              14

United Nations Office for South-South Cooperation (UNOSSC), hosted by United Nations
               Development Programme since 1974, was established by the UN General Assembly to
               promote coordinate South-South and triangular cooperation in the world.

    World Economic Forum

           What:

                 Established in 1971, the World Economic Forum (WEF) is an independent non-profit
                 organization that brings together business, political, and intellectual leaders to work on
                improving global conditions and people’s lives.

          Why:

                           It was founded as "European Management Forum" as a Non-profit foundation.

              The European Management Forum was the first non-governmental institution to initiate a
                 partnership with China’s economic development commissions, spurring economic reform
                  policies in China.

                   In 1987, the European Management Forum became the World Economic Forum and sought
                  to broaden its vision to include providing a platform for dialogue.

               Tell me more:

                Reports released by WEF:

                    Global Risks Report

                    Global Competitiveness Report

                    Global Gender Gap Report

    The Australia Group

           The Australia Group (AG) is an informal forum of countries which, through the harmonisation of
             export controls, seeks to ensure that exports do not contribute to the development of chemical
             or biological weapons.

                     It was established in 1985 after the use of chemical weapons by Iraq in 1984.

     Asian Development Bank

             Established in 1966, the Asian Development Bank was conceived in the early 1960s as a
               financial institution that would be Asian in character and foster economic growth and
             cooperation in one of the poorest regions in the world.

           As a multilateral development finance institution, ADB provides loans, technical assistance, and
             grants to its members.
